absent: Full definitions, sizes and initial values of tracing context, fault page, delayed release, page hash, global lock and notifier block objects.
Probe registration, fault entry, rearm routine, hash function and scheduler read section acquisition paired with the post trap release.
Canonical address test, syscall page test, user limit values, page size and virtual width discovery timing.
Platform capability values, vendor identifiers, encryption masks, device DMA limit fields and IOMMU selection outcome.
Bounce buffer default size and adjustment effects, secure timestamp preparation, feature log strings and virtio restriction callback contract.
RMP enable flag, probed base and size, segment sizes, table counts, bookkeeping size and early remap contract.
Firmware and kexec memory map types, propagation rules and early reservation query semantics.
Early page flag values, page table install helper, flush scope, boot parameter layout and command line size.
Control register and PAT layouts, cache invalidation scope, work area allocation and inner worker relocation offset.
Protection map size and encrypted constructor, early encrypted range helper and page count to byte conversion width.
Shared versus private transition helpers, hypercall number and arguments, and kexec begin and finish contracts.
Debug trap codes, step bit values, notifier return codes and registration API.
Entropy source, compatibility and randomize flags, guard gap, sysctl default and unmapped base computation.

findings.text: The tracing component provides start and stop operations that prepare a hash of fault pages and register a debug trap observer, then unregister the observer and warn when any hash bucket remains occupied at teardown.

Memory confidentiality support exposes queries and early setup operations that decide when DMA must avoid encrypted addresses, refresh bounce buffers and firmware state, scale bounce capacity from total memory, tag page protections as encrypted, and map or unmap low boot data and its command line.

Architecture helpers expose a probe safe kernel read admissibility test with two build variants, task size queries for compatibility and full address space modes, and a randomized mmap offset provider that selects width based on execution mode.

Secure nested paging host setup exposes an early memory map repair operation, and the boot encryption stub exposes a position independent routine that encrypts the kernel in place using caller supplied views, length, work area and page tables.

The debug exception observer only reacts to debug traps carrying a single step indication, delegates to the post trap handler, clears the step indication when handling completes, and otherwise lets notification continue.

Guest encryption attribute changes are driven through prepare and finish hooks plus flush requirement queries that the early SME setup installs into platform operations for later memory management use.
The post trap path serializes the liveness check and rearming of the current fault page under a global spin lock to avoid racing with concurrent release of that page.
The deferred removal path disables interrupts and holds the same global spin lock while walking the pending release chain and either unlinking idle pages or detaching busy ones.
Fault page reclamation is two stage: a first deferred pass separates idle from busy pages, then a second deferred pass frees only pages whose reference count is zero along with the container.

When no per CPU context is active the trap is treated as unexpected and ignored after a warning; when active the saved flag word is restored with single step cleared, nesting is decremented to zero with the scheduler read section released, and success is reported only when single step remains clear.

One build variant admits only addresses at or above the user limit, while the fuller variant also rejects the user guard page and the special syscall page, permits everything before virtual width discovery for early decoding, and otherwise requires a canonical address.

DMA is forced to unencrypted addresses for confidential guests, and for encrypted hosts only when the device lacks IOMMU translation and its coherent and bus limits fall within the encryption bit range.

Initialization does nothing without memory encryption, otherwise it refreshes bounce attributes, prepares secure time, and logs features; architectural setup first repairs host nested paging maps, then for guests scales bounce buffers to about six percent of memory clamped between default and one gigabyte and constrains virtio to restricted access.

Host map repair branches on the segmented table enable flag: segmented mode repairs around a probed base, bookkeeping area and each mapped segment from a temporarily mapped table, while contiguous mode repairs around base and end; each repair is skipped when already two megabyte aligned, otherwise the enclosing two megabyte RAM range is converted to reserved in firmware, kexec and normal maps and in the early allocator when not yet reserved.

Early boot data mapping walks in two megabyte steps creating or clearing entries derived from early flags with encryption removed, then flushes local translation caches; the wrappers do nothing without host encryption and preserve the command line address across the unmap by reading it first and across the map by reading it after.

For secure nested paging guests the transition to shared is performed before clearing encryption and the transition to private after establishing encryption, while hosts without memory encryption issue a hypercall on completion with the byte length derived from page count.
Translation flush is always reported as required for encryption changes, while cache flush is required only when the coherent encryption capability is absent.

Early SME setup tags early and supported page flags as encrypted, refreshes the protection map, installs prepare, finish, flush and kexec hooks, disables parallel startup under extended state encryption, disables compatibility syscalls under secure encryption, replaces ROM discovery and interrupt and DMI hooks under secure nested paging with no operation or SNP specific setup, and marks time as reliable under secure timestamping.
Protection initialization applies the encrypted attribute to every cached protection combination, and the early encrypted setter is a narrow wrapper that forces the encrypted direction.

The boot encryptor builds a private stack and a relocated copy of an inner worker outside the kernel image, then the worker switches page tables, refreshes global translations, saves and narrows caching attributes, invalidates caches, encrypts in place by double copying through an intermediate buffer in bounded chunks while advancing both views, and finally restores caching attributes and returns on the original stack.

Task limits are fixed for compatibility mode and selectable between default window and full space for sixty four bit mode; stack and mmap randomization are gated on the randomize flag with masked and shifted entropy, legacy layout follows personality or a sysctl, and the mmap top is derived from stack limit plus randomization and guard clamped between a floor and five sixths of task size with page alignment, while legacy bases add entropy to a per task unmapped origin.

The tracing state comprises a per CPU record holding an activity nesting count, an optional probe with optional completion callback, a current fault page and saved flags, plus fault pages carrying a reference count, hash linkage, release chain linkage and a pending release mark, grouped by a delayed container holding a chain head and a deferred free head.

Low boot parameters carry a split command line address whose low and extended halves combine into a physical pointer, and virtual address alignment state carries a flag word that boots with all bits set.

Trap handling moves from trap filter to active check to optional probe completion to locked rearm to flag restore and nesting teardown, ending either as unhandled when inactive or externally stepped, or as handled when the single step indication was owned and cleared.
Pending pages start marked for release, then under lock either remain marked and leave the hash when idle toward deferred free, or become unmarked and detached when busy to await a later cycle.

Encryption attribute updates flow from early request through prepare invalidation for shared transitions to page table update and finish validation for private transitions with conditional hypercall notification.

Surprise traps without context signal external debugger interference or logic error, leftover hash entries at teardown foreshadow memory leaks for later tracing, and admitting user, guard or special syscall addresses to fault free kernel reads risks unhandled faults.

Unaligned confidential table placement risks fatal faults and kexec reuse of its range unless enclosed in a reserved two megabyte window, scanning unvalidated ROM on secure nested paging guests risks crashes, and unfiltered compatibility syscall entry under secure encryption risks hypervisor driven abuse.
Segment table entries encode mapped extent in the low twenty bits and segment base in bits twenty through fifty one.

Layout constants fix the minimum mmap to stack gap at one hundred twenty eight megabytes, select per mode entropy widths from shared or compatibility specific controls depending on build, guard the internal memory header with a dedicated preprocessor symbol, and start alignment flags with all bits set.
